item.title: Second-Order Differential Equations
item.description: A second-order circuit obeys \frac{d^2x}{dt^2} + 2\alpha\frac{dx}{dt} + \omega_0^2 x = f.

item.title: Source Transformation
item.description: A voltage source V_s in series with a resistor R behaves exactly the same, from the outside, as a current source I_s = \frac{V_s}{R} in parallel with the same R.

item.title: Damping in Series and Parallel RLC
item.description: Damping is how quickly a resistor drains away the energy swinging between L and C.

item.title: LC Oscillation
item.description: When an inductor and a capacitor are connected together, energy passes back and forth between them, so the voltage and current oscillate as sine waves at \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}.

item.title: Capacitors and Inductors
item.description: Capacitors and inductors are the two energy-storage elements: a capacitor stores energy in an electric field set up by its voltage, and an inductor stores energy in a magnetic field set up by its current.

item.title: Ch 5: Operational Amplifiers
item.description: Overview Readings Alexander & Sadiku, Ch 5 An operational amplifier (op amp) takes the voltage difference between its two inputs, multiplies it by a very large gain, and outputs the result.
